card.summary: H.R. 7148, titled the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026, became Public Law No. 119-75 on February 3, 2026. This federal law provides funding for the Department of Defense, Departments of Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education, as well as Transportation, Housing and Urban Development, and related agencies for fiscal year 2026. It also sets guidelines for the U.S. Sentencing Commission, extends various healthcare, Medicaid, Medicare, and trade programs, introduces pharmacy benefit management transparency rules, and awards a payment to the widow of a late representative.

summary: H.R. 6500, enacted as Public Law 119-103, is a temporary funding and extension measure. It provides continuing fiscal year 2027 appropriations for federal agencies and programs through December 11, 2026, to prevent a government shutdown. It also extends various expiring authorizations, including agricultural and trade programs, surface transportation programs, and numerous Department of Veterans Affairs health care, housing, and benefit authorities.

affected_groups.effect: Receives temporary funding through December 11, 2026, maintaining operations at FY2026 levels and avoiding a government shutdown.
Extends specific VA health care programs, housing assistance, suicide prevention grants, caregiver support, and homeless assistance programs through December 11, 2026.
Extends federal surface transportation programs, Appalachian Regional Commission activities, and highway trust fund expenditure authorities through December 11, 2026.
Extends duty-free market access and trade preferences under the African Growth and Opportunity Act and Haiti Economic Lift Program through December 31, 2028.

key_provisions: Provides continuing FY2027 appropriations for federal agencies and programs through the earlier of December 11, 2026, or the enactment of applicable appropriations acts, generally funding programs at FY2026 levels.

Extends agricultural, grain inspection, and foreign assistance authorities, including the United States Grain Standards Act, Food for Peace, and the African Growth and Opportunity Act through December 31, 2028.
Extends surface transportation programs, highway and transit trust fund expenditure authorities, and related funding availability deadlines through late 2026 and 2027.

Extends numerous Department of Veterans Affairs programs and authorities—such as homeless veteran grants, suicide prevention grant programs, and housing adaptation assistance—through December 11, 2026.
Extends various cybersecurity, information-sharing authorities, and agency user fee collections (such as those for the EPA and Patent and Trademark Office) through December 11, 2026.
Temporarily delays portions of the new statutory definition of hemp and exempts the budgetary effects of Divisions B through D from statutory PAYGO rules.
missing_information: The precise total dollar amount appropriated by the continuing resolution division is not explicitly stated in the source text, as it relies on previous fiscal year funding levels.

summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 6500, enacted as Public Law 119-103, is a temporary funding and extension measure. It provides continuing fiscal year 2027 appropriations for federal agencies and programs through December 11, 2026, to prevent a government shutdown. It also extends various expiring authorizations, including agricultural and trade programs, surface transportation programs, and numerous Department of Veterans Affairs health care, housing, and benefit authorities.
summary_detail.significance: The law affects the entire federal government and a broad array of public programs by maintaining funding and authority temporarily through late 2026, preventing a federal government shutdown while giving Congress more time to pass full-year appropriations bills and reauthorize major expiring laws.
